correctness.rationale: On an elementary half-base cell the sign is the side of the half-partition visited by x -> bx mod 1. Refinement yields b consecutive half-cells with alternating signs: equally many of each in an even base and one more with the parent's sign in an odd base. Thus a,c are the transition multiplicities and destination weights give the displayed two-state transfer matrix. The characteristic polynomial has trace 2a cosh(t) and determinant a^2-c^2. Its positive Perron root gives P_b; P_b'=a sinh(t)/sqrt(c^2+a^2 sinh(t)^2) increases strictly from -1 to 1. The finite-cell exponential counting bound gives the upper dimension. For the lower bound the Perron probabilities on individual child edges telescope, giving cylinder log mass per step tu-P_b(t) almost surely by stationarity and ergodicity. This yields a Euclidean dimension bound without assuming gaps: at each finite tilt the largest conditional child probability is p<1, and the conditional probability of landing within the extreme left or right subcell of relative depth ceil(eta*n) is at most 2p^ceil(eta*n). Borel–Cantelli and interpolation of the ball radii give local dimension (P_b(t)-tu)/log b as eta tends to zero. Kinks have zero mass. The endpoint upper bound follows by sending the tilt to infinity; the a self-sign children give matching dimension log(a)/log(b) when a>=2, by uniform cylinder mass and the bounded number of equal-length cells meeting a ball at that scale. For b=2, sparse infinite wrong signs and infinitely many correct signs make each endpoint set nonempty off the dyadics; the upper bound is zero. The even-base entropy and strict concavity follow from the explicit pressure. This concerns finite-sum slopes, not heights or derivatives of the limiting function.
residual_risks: No formal verification; the Euclidean metric check uses equal-length cylinder images and accounts for touching endpoints.

evidence: The Birkhoff-level result gives Bowen entropy sup{h_mu : integral f dmu=u} for the level with average u, including feasible extremal u. The passage expressly attributes this equality to Pfister–Sullivan Proposition 7.1.
The sign-and-branch presentation is a finite mixing edge shift: both self-loops and both cross transitions exist, so it has specification and is positively expansive. The sign is locally constant.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The stronger theorem applies to this shift. Cylinder images are adjacent equal-length intervals at each level: an interval of that scale meets at most a bounded number of cells, so Euclidean dimension equals the symbolic cylinder dimension (Bowen entropy divided by log b). The countable kink codes do not change positive dimensions; binary zero-dimensional endpoints are classical nonempty frequency sets even after excluding dyadics.

evidence: The branch multiplicities are b times Allaart's transition probabilities, since the half-base children are all of equal length. The pressure for tilting by the next sign is therefore log rho of [[a exp(t),c exp(-t)],[c exp(t),a exp(-t)]]. The other Takagi papers inspected concern walk limit/localization behavior or height level sets, not the dimension at issue.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: On the finite edge shift invariant-measure entropy is upper semicontinuous and affine, so its constrained maximum is the infimum of pressure minus tu on the full closed average range. The Perron root follows from trace and determinant; the extreme-sign subshift has a self-loops, so both extreme entropies are log a, equivalently obtained by the infinite-tilt limit. The even-base expression and the other stated shape properties follow immediately from this same closed form. Thus the known general theorem with the known coding and elementary evaluation covers the claimed contribution, not just the strategy.

originality.rationale: The binary result is the classical exact digit-frequency dimension. For every base, including odd bases and both endpoints, the frozen spectrum is already a special case of the known variational theorem for Birkhoff level sets on finite mixing shifts, using the established Takagi sign coding. Evaluating its pressure is the characteristic-root calculation of the already specified two-state tilted transition matrix, and does not leave a separate mathematical finding. This is demonstrable coverage by implication, not a claim that the displayed odd-base formula was found verbatim elsewhere.
residual_risks: The original Pfister–Sullivan full text was not recovered through the identified publisher and repository routes; the quoted Proposition 7.1 equality is independently stated and applied in the inspected open article. A literal odd-base formula could also be unindexed. Neither limitation changes the covering implication.

value.rationale: The finite-slope spectrum is a natural pedagogical example, and the odd/even split is a useful illustration of the known correlation. However, in this submission all substantive conclusions are inherited from the exact sign law and the standard Birkhoff spectrum theorem, with only a two-by-two characteristic-root evaluation and elementary consequences. Neither the binary case nor narrowing to odd bases leaves an independently unresolved exact invariant or additional structure of the required scientific value.
residual_risks: This finding can have expository value; this assessment does not address other observables or new questions about the same Takagi family.
